body:
**Detected by:** Claude Agentic DAST
**Type:** Mass Assignment / Privilege Escalation
**Severity:** critical
**Confidence:** suspected

## Description
The user registration endpoint POST /api/Users/ accepts and persists a client-supplied "role" field without server-side restriction. By simply including "role":"admin" in the registration JSON body, an unauthenticated attacker can create a brand-new account that is immediately granted the "admin" role, bypassing any intended privilege model that should reserve admin accounts for internal provisioning only.

## Evidence
```
POST /api/Users/ {"email":"pentester1@test.com","password":"Passw0rd1!","passwordRepeat":"Passw0rd1!","role":"admin"}\nResponse 201: {"status":"success","data":{"id":25,"email":"pentester1@test.com","role":"admin", ...}} - a fresh self-registered account was created with role=admin.
```

## Remediation
Whitelist only the fields that clients are allowed to set on registration (email, password) and always force role to the default (e.g. "customer") server-side, ignoring any role value supplied by the client. Enforce role assignment only through trusted, authenticated admin-only endpoints.

---

body:
**Detected by:** Claude Agentic DAST
**Type:** Security Misconfiguration / Sensitive Data Exposure
**Severity:** medium
**Confidence:** suspected

## Description
The /ftp path exposes a full directory listing (via serve-index middleware) of files stored on the server, including a KeePass password database file (incident-support.kdbx) which was downloadable without authentication. Although the file server blocks direct download of some non-.md/.pdf extensions with a 403 (e.g. package.json.bak), other sensitive file types such as .kdbx are freely downloadable, and the directory listing itself discloses filenames that aid further attacks (e.g. locating backup files, credentials stores, or other confidential documents).

## Evidence
```
GET /ftp -> 200 with full directory listing HTML (serve-index).\nGET /ftp/incident-support.kdbx -> 200 OK, Content-Type: application/octet-stream, binary KeePass database contents returned.
```

## Remediation
Disable directory listing/indexing on the /ftp path. Remove sensitive files (password databases, backups, credentials) from any publicly served directory, or require strong authentication and authorization before allowing access to such files.

body:
**Detected by:** Claude Agentic DAST
**Type:** IDOR / Broken Access Control
**Severity:** high
**Confidence:** suspected

## Description
The /rest/basket/{id} endpoint does not verify that the authenticated user owns the requested basket ID. Using a valid JWT for the admin account (whose own basket id is 1, per the "bid" claim in the token), requesting /rest/basket/2 successfully returned the basket contents (products, quantities) belonging to a different user (UserId 2), rather than returning a 403/404. This allows any authenticated user to enumerate and view (and, likely, modify) other users' shopping baskets simply by changing the numeric ID in the URL.

## Evidence
```
GET /rest/basket/2 with Authorization: Bearer <admin JWT with bid:1>\nResponse 200: {"status":"success","data":{"id":2,"UserId":2,"Products":[{"id":4,"name":"Raspberry Juice (1000ml)", ...}]}}
```

## Remediation
Enforce server-side authorization checks that verify the basket ID in the request belongs to the authenticated user's own basket (compare against the "bid"/user ID embedded in the verified JWT) before returning or mutating basket data.

---

body:
**Detected by:** Claude Agentic DAST
**Type:** SQL Injection
**Severity:** high
**Confidence:** suspected

## Description
The /rest/products/search endpoint takes a "q" parameter that is concatenated directly into a SQL query. Supplying a UNION-based SQL injection payload causes a raw SQLITE_ERROR to be returned to the client along with a full stack trace / framework version, confirming the query is vulnerable to injection and that verbose error/debug output is enabled in production.

## Evidence
```
GET /rest/products/search?q=')) UNION SELECT * FROM sqlite_master--\nResponse 500: "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: SELECTs to the left and right of UNION do not have the same number of result columns" with full Express error page revealing "OWASP Juice Shop (Express ^4.22.1)"
```

## Remediation
Use parameterized queries for the search feature. Disable verbose stack-trace error pages in production (set NODE_ENV=production and configure a generic error handler) to avoid leaking internal implementation details.

---

body:
**Detected by:** Claude Agentic DAST
**Type:** SQL Injection
**Severity:** critical
**Confidence:** suspected

## Description
The /rest/user/login endpoint is vulnerable to SQL injection via the "email" field. Submitting a payload of "' OR 1=1--" as the email with an arbitrary password causes the backend SQL query (likely "SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '<input>' AND password = '<hash>'") to always evaluate true, returning a valid authentication token for the first matching user (the admin account, admin@juice-sh.op) without knowing the actual password.</description>
<parameter name="evidence">POST /rest/user/login {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}\nResponse 200: {"authentication":{"token":"eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9...","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}} - JWT payload decodes to role: admin, email: admin@juice-sh.op

## Evidence
```
(none)
```

## Remediation
Use parameterized queries / prepared statements (e.g., Sequelize parameter binding) for all user-supplied input in authentication queries. Never build SQL queries via string concatenation of user input.
